context:
Goal: design fixes ride the normal review rounds, and a screen changed later still gets a design read (your 204 a).
Problem (rule): decision design-agents puts the design reviewer beside code round 1. A second design read runs only if a later round changed a screen's "layout". That word is the coordinator's reading, and the record does not define it.
Based on (read): #1231 merged Nov 5 06:36 CST with the coordinator's reading.
Departs from: main (a second read on an undefined "layout" change) — a and b define it, c drops it. Your answer rewrites one line of decision design-agents.

options.gain: No screen change merges unseen by a designer.
options.how: Markup, styles, or the tokens a screen uses: any change gets one more design read.
options.label: Any change to a screen file after round 1
options.lose: A design read for small style fixes too.

options.how: An element added, removed or moved, or a size or spacing change.
options.label: Only a change in structure
options.lose: Someone must judge what counts, so a change can slip by.

options.how: The code reviewer alone checks the design findings after round 1.
options.label: Never
options.lose: A late screen change gets no designer's eye.

short: When does a second design read run?
title: After code round 1, what screen change gets a second design review?
why: Recommended: a. It needs no judgment call, and no screen change merges unseen.
